This introduces many exciting choices: Serve this here? Those cards there? Do I open a new trick? With so many options you need to plan ahead carefully and find the right time to secure the most points. Can you predict the number of tricks you will win? There are other trick prediction games, but none where you must watch up to 4 tricks at the same time. Make exactly the number of tricks you predict, not one too many, nor one too few. If you lose your concentration for even a minute, your wily opponents will take your tricks away. The winner is the player who has the most victory points at the end of three rounds. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Can you predict the number of tricks you will win? There are other trick prediction games, but none where you must watch up to 4 tricks at the same time. Make exactly the number of tricks you predict, not one too many, nor one too few. If you lose your concentration for even a minute, your wily opponents will take your tricks away... The winner is the player who has the most victory points at the end of three rounds. Contents 1 Game Components 2 Game Flow 3 Trick Taking 3.1 Rules for placing cards and taking tricks 4 End of a Round 5 Game End Game Components 60 playing cards (numbered 1-15, in four colors) 20 markers (4 in each color) 45 victory points cards (9 in each color) Game Flow The game is played over three rounds. Each round proceeds in the following order: Shuffle the playing cards (24,36, 48 or 60 cards, depending on the number of players), and deal 12 to each player. Each player looks at their cards and decides in which order to place their three victory points cards in front of them. For the first round, each player has the three victory points cards with one "pin" on the bottom and the numbers 1, 2, and 3. For the second round, each player has the three victory points cards with two "pins" on the bottom and the numbers 2, 4, and 6. For the third round, each player has the three victory points cards with three "pins" on the bottom and the numbers 3, 6, and 9. Each player places the three victory points cards upside down in a row from left to right in front of them. The order they place the cards depends on how many tricks they think they can win during this round (see below). All players play their playing cards following the rules explained in the "Trick Taking" section (see below). After 12 turns, the round is over. Each player takes the victory points card they won and places it right side up beside them. Continue to the next round. The game ends after three rounds. Trick Taking In the first round, the oldest player starts. In subsequent rounds, the player to the left of the previous starting player starts. The game is played in clockwise rotation until the round ends, after 12 turns. On each turn a player plays exactly one card. The player can either play the card on an already opened trick, or open a new trick. (Note: No more than four open tricks are allowed at one time.) Each trick should form its own pile, and cards played on a trick should be placed so that the value of each card in the trick is visible. Whoever begins a new trick places their marker beside it to claim it. Any subsequent player who plays a higher card of the same color on this trick returns the marker to its owner and places their own marker on it. Rules for placing cards and taking tricks When placing a card on a trick, players must follow the color of the first card played on that trick. Players can only play a card of a different color on a trick if there is no other place on the table where the different-colored card could be played. However, a player may choose to play a card of a different color on a trick (if allowed) even if that player could play a correctly colored card on that or another trick. [Rating: 3/10] Precision bidder where your bid value rotates as you take tricks. You play to a few simultaneous tricks. It's okay I guess. I don't know, there are so many other games I'd rather play than this one.

[Rating: 4/10] I'm not sure if there's anything that makes this better than other trick-takers, but I like it.  It's basically a bidding game with multiple simultaneous tricks.  I'm not a huge fan of bidding games, but I think I like this one better than most.  Probably a keeper.

[Rating: 4/10] Nice idea to serve up to four tricks at the same time.  But for my taste in the end too little control and too much dependent on luck.

[Rating: 5/10] I'm not a trick-taking guy.. otherwise i would've rated this higher. I like the ease of the betting mechanic, how many tricks you make..  Artwork & component quality is good.

[Rating: 5/10] High quality cards and a really weird approach to trick-taking. I'm not sure there's enough skill involved to make this a keeper though.

[Rating: 5/10] Nice twist on trick taking that works well. Makes for great comebacks. Lots of take that opportunities.

[Rating: 5/10] Having four separate tricks open at the same time gives you quite a bit more leeway to get rid of unwanted cards. On the other hand, it is quite a bit easier to pass unwelcome tricks to people because in many cases you do not have to follow suit. Maybe this balances out in the end. In general, however, it seems to lead to rounds that only become interesting towards the end, when it becomes more difficult to dodge unwanted tricks.

[Rating: 5/10] The deck consists of standard colored suits and values with no special cards. Each player also has three sets of bidding cards with different values that must be arranged face-down after the hands are dealt. In the first round, the bidding cards have a value of 1, 2, and 3 and can be put in any order, such as 2-3-1. When you win trick, you turn over your first bidding card, here giving 2 points. Winning the next trick means you flip down the 2 and turn up the three. In that way you go left to right and start back again if you hit the end. [Rating: 5/10] Each hand starts strong but ends slow due to the nature of being able to have 4 tricks at a time; it makes it so you can easily avoid tricks late in the hand. I like the idea but the execution is a bit underwhelming. Artwork is super fun and cute

[Rating: 5/10] Nice game, but really nothing special. I have to say though - I bought this and Skull King at the same time, so this game had a rough time since i compared it to its (imho way better) Trick-taking brother all the time.

[Rating: 5/10] A fun trick taking game with cute art. It might be a nice step up with kids or new people to the genre. Not a "serious" game as you don't seem to have control over things with those simultaneous tricks being played and that can affect your predictions. Still, a very nice and fresh idea overall.
